description: An Algerian Young Team already winning national and international Hackathon
summary: Every season, farmers bet a whole year on a crop rotation chosen from memory, while NASA satellites have recorded what their exact field lived through for 25 years. ITZA is a flight simulator for crop rotations: draw your field, and it reads that field's history from NASA data (POWER weather, MODIS and HLS vegetation, SMAP soil moisture, IMERG rainfall, NASADEM terrain), replays every real past season, and plausible 2050 seasons from NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6, on each candidate rotation, then shows which one held up best and why. Every number carries its NASA source, resolution and date, gaps are shown as gaps, and results are validated against public USDA records. It turns NASA's long Earth record into a rehearsal any farmer or advisor can run on a phone before committing a season, answering the "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ITZA lets a farmer rehearse crop rotations against the real weather their own field has already lived through.

1. Draw your field on a satellite map, or open one of the demo fields (Sétif, Algeria; Akron, Colorado, USA).

2. Field memory: 25 years of MODIS (250 m) and HLS (30 m) vegetation greenness reveal which seasons were cropped, fallow or bare. The farmer confirms or corrects this.

3. 3D field twin: NASADEM elevation becomes a 3D relief model; a rain simulation shows where water runs and collects on the real slopes, with the NASA vegetation time-lapse draped over it.

4. Season replay: every candidate rotation is simulated day by day through all 17 real seasons (2008–2025) with the FAO-56 crop water standard and a daily soil-water balance, plus heat, frost and erosion stress.

5. 2050: the same seasons are replayed under NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 projections (SSP1-2.6 / 2-4.5 / 3-7.0), labelled as scenarios, not forecasts.

6. Evidence cards: the best rotation, the runner-up and today's practice, each with why, evidence, benefits, information gaps, risks to check locally, and a confidence level.

7. Ask ITZA: a visual assistant answers questions ("Why is this rotation ranked first?") with interactive answer cards whose numbers all come from the engine.

HOW IT WORKS

- Data: NASA POWER, MODIS and CMR are called directly from the browser. Earthdata products (SMAP, IMERG, HLS, GRACE, NASADEM) are clipped and summarized per field by a FastAPI science service on Google Cloud Run using the Earthdata login.

- Engine: a pure TypeScript simulation in a Web Worker, with a fixed random seed and 200 Monte Carlo runs for uncertainty. Sliders re-rank rotations instantly, and the demo fields work fully offline as an installable app (PWA).

- Provenance: every value carries its dataset, version, resolution and date (for example "MOD13Q1 · 250 m · 2016-01-17"). Missing data is shown, never filled in silently. All formulas are published on the in-app Sources page.

- Machine learning as a second opinion: a LightGBM stress model trained on 5,085 real MODIS/POWER/SMAP pixel-seasons (spatial and leave-one-year-out cross-validation, SHAP explanations) and NASA/IBM Prithvi-EO-2.0 (experimental crop/fallow map) are compared with the engine, and disagreements are shown.

- Assistant: a hosted language model behind our own Cloudflare gateway only chooses tools and phrases the answer. Numbers come from the engine and NASA POWER/CMR tools, and every answer must fit a fixed set of answer components.

VALIDATION (shown as measured, including where we fall short)

- The rule engine, the ML model and satellite observations agree on 79% of seasons.

- On the Akron proof field, the inferred crop history matches the USDA Cropland Data Layer in 78% of seasons (target 80%). The rotation ranking is also compared with a long-term USDA-ARS trial, and it disagrees with the trial's direction; we show this honestly.

- Model skill and limits are documented in a public model card.

BENEFITS

- Turns NASA's 25-year Earth record into a decision a farmer can see in minutes, for any field on Earth, for free, on a phone.

- Built for drylands facing climate change, such as Algeria's high plains, and transferable anywhere NASA data exists.

- Options, not orders: no yield guarantees, and no fertilizer, pesticide or irrigation prescriptions. People decide.

WHAT WE HOPE TO ACHIEVE

Put a "flight simulator" in the hands of smallholder farmers and agricultural advisors, so the next rotation is chosen from evidence, not guesswork, before a season is lost.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React 19, Vite, TanStack Router and Query, Zustand, Tailwind, MapLibre GL, deck.gl, three.js, ECharts; Python 3.13, FastAPI, xarray, uv; LightGBM, SHAP, scikit-learn, TerraTorch (Prithvi-EO-2.0); Cloudflare Workers, Vercel AI SDK, A2UI; Google Cloud Run, Cloud Storage, Secret Manager; GitHub Actions. No special hardware.
